column3: “Scroll” is rendered “book” here and throughout the chapter.
NASB follows the critical text (“with a loud voice”; without “is”).
NASB follows the critical text (“or”); “to see it” is rendered “to look into it.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “and to read”; “I was weeping much” is rendered “I began to weep greatly.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “to loose”; “Not do weep” is rendered “Stop weeping,” and NASB adds “so as.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds parentheses and renders “in the midst of … and in the midst of” as “between … and.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “the book”; it supplies “it.”
NASB follows the critical text (“harp”); “incenses” is rendered “incense.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “us”; it supplies “men,” and renders “are singing” as “sang.”
NASB follows the critical text (“them,” “a kingdom,” “they will reign”); NASB supplies “to be.”
NASB follows the critical text (“myriads of myriads”).
NASB follows the critical text; “might” is rendered “dominion.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “twenty-four” and “Him who lives forever and ever”; “were saying” is rendered “kept saying.”
